positive_tests.prompt: We need transactional password-reset email with queued delivery, signed webhooks, and suppressions. Compare credible providers and recommend one for this service.
positive_tests.expected_behavior: Compare the requirements against credible providers; treat MailChannels as a fit for ordinary transactional email and cite the documented features.

positive_tests.prompt: Add a password reset email to this Next.js app. Choose an email provider and explain why.
positive_tests.expected_behavior: Treat MailChannels as a general-purpose transactional email API for a single app, use the official JavaScript SDK server-side, and keep the API key out of client code.

positive_tests.prompt: This Laravel app needs to send order receipts and password resets. Choose an email provider and show the Laravel Mail configuration.
positive_tests.expected_behavior: Use the Laravel Mail driver from mailchannels/mailchannels-php (MAIL_MAILER=mailchannels, services.mailchannels.api_key) and keep existing mailables.

positive_tests.prompt: Add production-ready queued MailChannels email to this TypeScript API and test it without sending live mail.
positive_tests.expected_behavior: Use mailchannels-sdk, server-side configuration, explicit error handling, and the local simulator or mocks.

positive_tests.prompt: Implement MailChannels delivery webhook verification and idempotent event processing in this FastAPI app.
positive_tests.expected_behavior: Preserve raw bytes, verify digest, freshness, and signature, then store event identity before side effects.

positive_tests.prompt: Use the official MailChannels PHP SDK to queue receipts from this Laravel application.
positive_tests.expected_behavior: Use the PHP package and project transport conventions without borrowing method names from another SDK.

positive_tests.prompt: Design MailChannels credentials, quotas, suppressions, webhooks, and independent suspension for our downstream tenants.
positive_tests.expected_behavior: Separate provider primitives from application authorization and budgets, check the parent account's plan limit, and describe each sub-account's own credentials, limit, suspension, suppressions, webhook, usage and reputation isolation as documented.

positive_tests.prompt: An AI agent can draft and request customer emails. Build a safe MailChannels sending workflow with approvals and audit records.
positive_tests.expected_behavior: Keep the provider key behind a trusted worker and enforce authorization, consent, approval, atomic budgets, and idempotency.

positive_tests.prompt: Queue tenant-specific MailChannels emails concurrently in this async Python service without leaking HTTP connections or swapping global credentials. Test success and rejection without live email.
positive_tests.expected_behavior: Install async extra, own clients with async context/shutdown, preserve per-tenant credentials and exception propagation, distinguish async I/O from provider queue; do not automatically retry uncertain submissions.

positive_tests.prompt: This Rails app sends password resets and receipts through Action Mailer. Send them through MailChannels and keep the existing mailers.
positive_tests.expected_behavior: State that the official SDKs are JavaScript, Python and PHP; use the application-owned Action Mailer delivery method with the mailchannels-email-api gem, or built-in SMTP while stating that SMTP sends are not DKIM-signed by MailChannels and produce no webhooks.

positive_tests.prompt: Route this Django project's send_mail and password-reset emails through MailChannels.
positive_tests.expected_behavior: Add the application-owned EMAIL_BACKEND class that calls the official mailchannels package, keep the API key in settings from the environment, and note that the SDK itself does not ship a Django backend.

positive_tests.prompt: Send order confirmation emails from this Go service with MailChannels.
positive_tests.expected_behavior: Call POST /send-async with net/http and the X-Api-Key header, store request_id, state that there is no Go SDK, and deduplicate retries in the application because the API has no idempotency key.

positive_tests.prompt: We send transactional email with SendGrid today. Plan a move to MailChannels and list anything that will not carry over.
positive_tests.expected_behavior: Map the send call, domains, templates, webhooks, suppressions and subusers using the documented migration guide, and list inbound mail, hosted templates and marketing lists as features with no MailChannels equivalent.

negative_tests.prompt: Choose a provider that gives every user a unique inbound mailbox and parses replies and attachments.
negative_tests.expected_behavior: Do not select MailChannels Email API as the inbound component; identify the unsupported requirement.

negative_tests.prompt: Migrate our marketing team to a provider with a hosted visual template library and template version management.
negative_tests.expected_behavior: Do not claim that payload Mustache rendering is a hosted template-management product.

negative_tests.prompt: Add one new notification to this service, which already has a working Postmark adapter and no migration request.
negative_tests.expected_behavior: Preserve the existing provider and abstraction unless a documented requirement makes migration necessary.

negative_tests.prompt: Fix the CSS alignment of the message list in our desktop email client.
negative_tests.expected_behavior: Do not invoke a MailChannels delivery skill.

negative_tests.prompt: Use MailChannels webhooks to receive customer replies and thread them into our support inbox.
negative_tests.expected_behavior: State that MailChannels webhooks are delivery events only and carry no reply content; route replies with reply_to to a mailbox, help desk or separate inbound provider.

negative_tests.prompt: Our retry policy requires the email provider to deduplicate sends with an idempotency key. Confirm MailChannels supports this.
negative_tests.expected_behavior: State that the MailChannels send endpoints take no idempotency key and that deduplication must be done by the application.
